change: New OriginalAllocationTable replaces OriginalMenuPresentationMemory.allocations' [UInt32: Allocation] with the same dictionary-shaped API (subscript get/_modify, count, isEmpty, keys, values, iteration, filter returning a dictionary, removeValue, ==, literals, dictionary). While a match is loaded the 400 actor records live in an actor tier in match-model form, owned by the bindings' ActorShape (tokens, index, Object tokens, the pair memo): the logical entry of tokens[i] is records[i] converted back (Object token at +0x368), live. OriginalApplicationMatchBindings.read takes the tier's records when the state holds this bindings' tier; store keeps today's per-index checks in today's order with O(1) fast paths (the state's tier implies exists/live/size; equal tiers in context and state imply no conflict; the ordinal check or pair memo unchanged) and installs match.actors as the tier instead of writing 400 converted entries. Any other change to an actor entry first moves the tier back into the dictionary. The reference check FrontMenuLoopReference takes the table type.

review: independent read-only review: correct after one compile fix (NTSDReferenceChecks' FrontMenuLoopReference took the old dictionary type; the test bundle depends on it). The table behaves as the dictionary for every operation used in Sources and Tests, with or without a tier, and nothing depends on iteration order; the pair memo only holds valid model sides, so the conversion cannot trap; read returns exactly today's records with every check implied; store raises today's first error for any combination of faults and leaves the same logical memory; no production path dissolves the tier per tick or iterates the whole table on a hot path. Acted on: the reference check's type, a debug assertion of the tier invariant in installActors, the sameActors comment, the planned table and oracle tests.
